clue.text: Weather front may become much to first person's liking

indicators.note: the letters of the first three words may become something else when rearranged, signalling a reshuffle

explanation.surface: A forecaster rather enjoys the arrival of a weather front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may become' is the anagram signal: WEATHERFRONTMAY is rearranged. 'May' looks like part of the signal but its letters are fodder too.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something exactly to the speaker's taste, the 'first person' being me.

clue.text: Executive officer found common bird first

indicators.note: first places the bird ahead of the word for common

parts.note: the adjutant is a large Asian stork
common, as in widespread, means general

explanation.surface: An officer is said to have spotted an ordinary bird before anyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' says the bird's name goes in front, though the clue gives 'common' before 'bird'.
explanation.definitionFit: This senior staff officer handles a commander's administration, an executive role in the army.

clue.text: Add to endless story

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: endless says the word for story loses its final letter

parts.note: a story is a tale

explanation.surface: A writer is told to tack something onto a story that never finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' removes the last E from TALE, leaving TAL.
explanation.definitionFit: To add up a column of figures is to sum it, a verb sense of the word.

clue.text: Hearing for at least the second time

definitions.text: Hearing for at least the second time

parts.words: Hearing for at least the second time
parts.note: a hearing here is a court case, and one held again after a first attempt is a repeat trial

explanation.surface: Someone listens to a piece of music again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hearing' suggests listening, but it is the legal sense: a case heard in court.
explanation.definitionFit: A case tried again in court after an earlier trial is heard for at least a second time.

clue.text: Bore gave in

definitions.meaning: a field bore a crop, meaning it produced one
to give in is to submit or surrender

explanation.surface: Someone tiresome finally surrendered.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both produced, as land produces a harvest, and surrendered to pressure.

clue.text: Ineffectual person abroad to lack the courage to do something

definitions.text: lack the courage to do something

parts.note: a feeble, ineffectual person is a wimp
someone abroad is out of the country

explanation.surface: A feeble traveller overseas loses the nerve to act.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means backing down from something through fear.

clue.text: The man's wrong about a coarse cloth

parts.note: the man is he, so the man's is he's

indicators.note: about means the word for wrong goes around the letter a

parts.note: a wrong is a sin

explanation.surface: A man is mistaken about a rough fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: HE'S comes first, then 'about' puts A inside SIN, giving SIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a rough woven fabric of jute or hemp, used for sacking.

clue.text: Notice address for worship

parts.note: an advertisement, or ad, is a notice
a formal address or speech is an oration

explanation.surface: A notice gives an address where people may worship.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep reverence and veneration, especially of a god, is a synonym of worship.

clue.text: Three brothers from lighthouse and pilot authority?

parts.note: the Trinity is a group of three
brethren is an old plural of brother

explanation.surface: Three siblings come from a body running lighthouses and pilots.
explanation.walkthrough: Trinity House is the body that runs lighthouses and pilotage in England and Wales; its governing members are called the Elder Brethren. The question mark flags the loose description.
explanation.definitionFit: The members of Trinity House, the English lighthouse and pilotage authority, are collectively called its brethren.

clue.text: Black line from very high-velocity winds

parts.note: jet is a deep glossy black
a stream is a continuous line, as of traffic or people

explanation.surface: A dark line is traced by fierce winds on a weather chart.
explanation.definitionFit: These are narrow bands of very fast air currents high in the atmosphere.

clue.text: Promises to pay about 1,000 coming back from Finland

indicators.note: coming back means the whole assembly is read in reverse
about means the promises to pay go around the thousand

parts.note: IOUs are written promises to pay a debt
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: IOUs worth about a thousand are returned from Finland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts M inside IOUS to make IMOUS; 'coming back' reverses that.
explanation.definitionFit: Suomi is the Finnish people's own name for their country.

clue.text: Bound to include everybody who corresponded

indicators.note: to include means the word for bound takes the word for everybody inside it

parts.note: bound, as with rope, means tied
everybody is all

explanation.surface: Someone is obliged to involve everyone who wrote letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to include' puts ALL inside TIED.
explanation.definitionFit: When two accounts match or agree, they are said to tally.

clue.text: Japanese art increasing, so to speak

definitions.text: Japanese art increasing, so to speak

parts.words: Japanese art increasing, so to speak
parts.note: increasing sizes are described as twofold or tenfold, so a Japanese art of folding paper could jokingly be called increasing

explanation.surface: A Japanese art form is said to be gaining popularity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'increasing' plays on '-fold' as in 'twofold': the craft is all about folds.
explanation.definitionFit: The traditional craft of folding paper into shapes comes from Japan.

clue.text: Electronic copper coin

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: An electronic coin made of copper.
explanation.definitionFit: It was an old French coin, and later the name for the European currency unit before the euro.

clue.text: Showed the way forward home first having made oneself comfortable

indicators.note: first places the word for home ahead of the word for showed the way

parts.note: a nest is a home
to show the way forward is to lead, so led

explanation.surface: A guide led the way home first before settling down cosily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' says NEST comes before LED, though the clue gives them the other way round.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle snugly into a warm, sheltered position is to cuddle in comfortably.

clue.text: Player gets 50 per cent after a struggle

indicators.note: after says the word for fifty per cent follows the struggle

parts.note: a scrum is a disorderly struggle
fifty per cent is a half

explanation.surface: A player takes half the winnings after a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: A scrum-half is a rugby position: the player who feeds the ball into the scrum.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a rugby position, a player who puts the ball into the scrum.

clue.text: Therefore loses nothing but a little bit of work

indicators.note: loses means the zero is dropped from the Latin word

parts.note: ergo is Latin for therefore
O is zero, or nothing

explanation.surface: Therefore one loses nothing but a little work.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a tiny physics unit of work or energy, one ten-millionth of a joule.

clue.text: One in the grips of abstainer found wall-climber making swift movement

indicators.note: in the grips of means the word for one is held inside the abstainer

parts.note: TT, teetotal, describes someone who abstains from alcohol
an is the indefinite article, meaning one
ivy is a plant that climbs walls

explanation.surface: A teetotaller grabbing a wall-climbing plant moves quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the grips of' puts AN inside TT, giving TANT, then IVY follows.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an old hunting cry or word for a headlong gallop at full speed.

clue.text: Going up and down with surprised expression

indicators.note: in a down clue, the entry reads the same going up as going down

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Someone bobbing up and down exclaims in surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a palindrome: read upwards or downwards in the grid, it is the same.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an exclamation of sudden discovery or triumph.

clue.text: Rubbish container in French station

indicators.note: in means the container sits inside the French word

parts.note: gare is French for a railway station
a bag is a container

explanation.surface: A rubbish bin is found in a French railway station.
explanation.definitionFit: It is waste or refuse, chiefly in American use.

clue.text: Disturbed bats are alongside

indicators.note: disturbed means the letters of the next two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: Disturbed bats fly side by side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disturbed' rearranges BATSARE.
explanation.definitionFit: It means side by side, level with something.

clue.text: Fifty found in French cave form a cultural group isolated in the country

definitions.text: a cultural group isolated in the country

parts.note: en is French for in

indicators.note: found here means the fifty is placed inside the cave

parts.note: taken as written
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Fifty people found in a French cave form an isolated community.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in French' gives EN; 'found' puts L inside CAVE to give CLAVE.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a distinct community or territory surrounded by a larger one.

clue.text: Gap runs behind sunken panel

indicators.note: behind says the R comes after the word for gap

parts.note: a lacuna is a gap
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A gap runs behind a recessed panel.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an architectural term for a coffered ceiling or one of its recessed panels.

clue.text: Catch ball under chimney, it's a pain

indicators.note: under says in this down clue that the catch and ball sit below the chimney

parts.note: lum is a Scottish word for a chimney
to catch is to bag
O is round, like a ball

explanation.surface: Catching a ball under the chimney hurts the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under' places BAG and O below LUM in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: It is pain in the lower back, a type of backache.

clue.text: Monstrous horseman

parts.note: a mythical monster that is part man and part horse could be called a horseman

explanation.surface: A frightening rider gallops into view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horseman' looks like a rider, but here the creature is literally horse and man in one.
explanation.definitionFit: This creature of Greek myth has a man's upper body and a horse's lower body.

clue.text: It's fun to jump around with the farmers' group initially

indicators.note: jump around means the letters of the word fun move about

explanation.surface: Farmers find it fun to jump around together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' signals an abbreviation: the National Farmers' Union, the main British farmers' organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the initials of the National Farmers' Union, the British farming trade body.

clue.text: Nice rum can be expressed as numbers

indicators.note: can be suggests the letters could become something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: The price of rum in Nice can be expressed in figures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be' rearranges NICERUM. 'Nice' is the French city, not the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: It means relating to or shown in figures.

clue.text: Finally stumped the pet

parts.note: a pet whose end has been stumped, cut short, would be a breed of feline with no tail

explanation.surface: In the end the pet left someone baffled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stumped' suggests puzzled, but it means cut to a stump: this breed from the Isle of Man is tailless.
explanation.definitionFit: The breed from the Isle of Man is known for having no tail.

clue.text: Most upset it had been divided

definitions.meaning: deeply distressed, as in being very hurt by news

explanation.surface: Most people were upset that it had been split.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both greatly distressed and chopped into pieces.

clue.text: Jack returns having caught one with a lasso

indicators.note: having caught means the reversed sailor holds the one inside
returns means the sailor word is read backwards

parts.note: a jack tar, or jack, is a sailor, so tar
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A sailor comes back having roped someone with a lasso.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' reverses TAR to RAT; 'having caught' puts I inside, giving RIAT; then A.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a long rope with a noose used for catching cattle, a lariat.

clue.text: A bloomer going round workroom producing gypsum

indicators.note: going round means A and the flower surround the workroom

parts.note: a bloomer is a flower, here the aster
a lab is a workroom

explanation.surface: A gaffe in the laboratory produces a mineral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' looks like a mistake, but it is a flower. 'going round' puts LAB inside A + ASTER.
explanation.definitionFit: This fine-grained white stone is a form of the mineral gypsum.

clue.text: Having received plenty of fresh-air, further discussion was made possible

definitions.meaning: literally letting outside air in through an unclosed entrance
figuratively keeping an opportunity available for talks

explanation.surface: After airing the room, the chairman allowed more talks.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally, an unclosed entrance lets air in; figuratively, the idiom means keeping an opportunity for talks.
